item.title: Leave politics to politicians, northern minorities tell clerics
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Northern Nigeria Minorities Group, NNMG, has cautioned religious leaders, particularly imams and pastors, against partisan political involvement and the use of churches and mosques as platforms for political mobilisation. The group, which represents more than 200 minority communities across Northern Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), urged religious leaders to distinguish their spiritual responsibilities from partisan political activities, warning that inflammatory political messages from religious platforms could heighten tensions and expose Nigerians to violence. Addressing journalists in Abuja yesterday, the Convener, Jacob Edi, also known as Kakaki Bassange, said religious leaders should focus on praying for the peace and unity of the country, while leaving partisan politics to politicians. He said: “Politics is for politicians, religion is for pastors and imams. They should pray for this nation. They should pray for the peace and unity of Nigeria. “When a pastor or an imam tells you about peace, he is not looking for your vote. He is not even looking for your money. This is his duty. This is his calling.” Edi said anyone interested in partisan politics should relinquish religious leadership and join a political party to pursue such ambitions. “If he wants to come into politics, he should remove the garment or remove the jalabia or whatever and go to any party,” he said. The group also cautioned opposition politicians against actions capable of destabilising the country, urging them to resolve political disagreements through constitutional and judicial processes. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselv

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn’t create success for our team this season.” Latest Ducks news Oregon makes a big leap in latest College Football Playoff rankings Dan Lanning backs expanded college football playoff to 24 teams Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham takes shot at Oregon’s $50M roster Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: ‘I Want To Fight Rodtang’ – Asadula Imangazaliev Eyes Potential World Grand Prix Final Against ‘The Iron Man’
item.description: Reigning ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Champion Asadula “The Dagestan Ninja” Imangazaliev has already conquered some of the division’s most formidable strikers. But there’s one superstar he’d relish the opportunity to face on the biggest stage. The undefeated Dagestani has expressed his interest in a potential showdown with former longtime divisional king Rodtang “The Iron Man” Jitmuangnon , a matchup that could materialize in the final of the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix. First, Imangazaliev must defend his gold against #1-ranked Aslamjon “El Pantera” Ortikov in a highly anticipated quarterfinal rematch at The Inner Circle 39 on Friday, November 20, live in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium. The action will stream exclusively for members at live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram Meanwhile, Rodtang begins his own tournament journey against fellow Thai legend Nong-O Hama at The Inner Circle 38 on November 13. The quarterfinal winner will advance to face either Shimon Yoshinari or Ramadan Ondash in the semifinals. That creates the possibility of an extraordinary final between two generations of flyweight Muay Thai greatness. And although Imangazaliev welcomes that possibility, he knows the star-studded bracket offers no guarantees. The undefeated Russian told onefc.com: “Yes, it would be very nice for me if Rodtang makes it. I want to fight Rodtang after Aslamjon. But things have changed a little bit, and I don’t know now. “It doesn’t matter. If I need to fight someone else, no problem. But [Ramadan] Ondash and Shimon are also a very good fight, two younger guys in this Grand Prix. Too much action, you know.” Photo credit: ONE Championship A potential meeting would carry immense significance for both men. Rodtang ruled the division for five years and became a global sensation through his relentless aggression, durability, and electrifying performances. Imangazaliev, meanwhile, has established himself as the division’s new standard-bearer, defeating Kongthoranee Sor Sommai , Nong-O, and Ortikov during his unbeaten rise to World Title glory. The Dagestani recognizes Rodtang’s legendary status, though he admits he cannot judge his potential rival’s current motivation from the outside. In his view, achieving enormous success can present athletes with a different kind of challenge. He said: “You know, when you have too much money, when you have everything, maybe you can get tired of the sport, of the discipline. You need to make weight. You need to train two times a day, every day. “But when you have everything, maybe when you wake up in the morning, you think, ‘I have everything. Why do I need this?’ And maybe he’s not hungry. But I don’t know. Maybe he’s still hungry too. But for me, it doesn’t matter, you know, because I’m hungry. I know inside I have fire. I’m ready.” View this post on Instagram That hunger has fueled Imangazaliev’s remarkable ascent through ONE, where he has combined spectacular finishes wit

item.title: Where are the meters?
item.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved a N30 billion disbursement to electricity distribution companies (DisCos) for the procurement and installation of meters under the meter acquisition fund (MAF) tranche C scheme. According to Order No NERC/2026/121, issued on Monday, the fund targets the provision of free meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerating installations for Band B consumers. The commission had approved N21 billion for the first tranche and N28 billion for the second tranche of the initiative. In the order, NERC said the funding would be shared among the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NDC alleges plot to disrupt Obi’s visit to Benue Nigeria’s states have more money. Are they spending it well? Daily Trust reports that since the introduction of reforms in the electricity sector under the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration, the federal government has granted approval for the procurement of N1.116trn worth of prepaid meters for distribution to consumers for free. The reform, which saw the removal of electricity subsidy for Band A electricity customers, was meant to provide free meters for customers under the band, with extension to others in Band B, C, D and E. But despite the approval and release of funds, the rollout of the meters has been slow. Though the government maintains that the country has 12,747,789 electricity customers with 8,045,565 customers metered and 4,704,224 unmetered, many Nigerians still pay for their meters to stop alleged extortion by electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) through estimated billing. To reduce reliance on estimated billing and improve electricity-sector revenue collection, the government introduced new schemes worth N1.11trn from 2024 to date. The distribution has largely focused on Band A customers, whom the former Minister of Power, Adebayo Adelabu, said made up 15 percent of electricity consumers. Daily Trust reports that the schemes the government introduced include the Distribution Sector Recovery Program (DISREP), Meters Acquisition Fund (MAF) and Presidential Metering Initiative (PMI). A breakdown of the money allocated to each scheme showed that DISREP allocated $250m (N337bn at N1348.10/dollar) for 3.2m meters, MAF got N79bn and PMI was allocated N700bn. While the DISREP and MAF are ongoing, PMI will start next year, but the funds have been released to the agency spearheading it. What the metering schemes entail DISREP is a $500 million World Bank loan aimed at improving the financial and technical performance of DisCos. One of the major objectives of DISREP is to close the metering gap in the NESI by deploying 3.2 million smart meters. Installation of meters under the DISREP commenced in May 2025. item.title: Nigeria’s private sector foreign debt rise 179.6% to $54.5bn — World Bank
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The World Bank said that the foreign debt of Nigerian companies rose by 179.6 per cent in seven years to $54.48 billion in 2025 from $19.49 billion in 2018. This implies that Nigerian businesses now owe foreign lenders almost three times what they owed in 2018. The World Bank disclosed this in its International Debt Report 2026 which stated that Nigeria’s private sector nonguaranteed external debt stood at $54.476 billion as of December 2025. The World Bank explained that the total external debt of a country is the sum of public and publicly guaranteed debt, private nonguaranteed debt, and short-term debt. According to the World Bank, private sector nonguaranteed external debt refers to money borrowed by private companies from foreign banks, investors and other lenders without the government or any public institution guaranteeing repayment. “Private nonguaranteed debt comprises long-term external obligations of private debtors that are not guaranteed by a public entity. “Public and publicly guaranteed external debt comprises long-term external obligations (maturities of over one year) of all public debtors, including debt held by the central government and by state-owned enterprises. Short-term debt is defined as debt with an original maturity of one year or less ,” the report said. The 179.6 per cent growth in Nigeria’s private sector in the seven years was faster than the increase in government-backed external debt, which rose by 155.5 per cent from $24.422 billion in 2018 to $62.4 billion in 2025. The World Bank report showed that private companies’ foreign debt is becoming an increasingly important part of Nigeria’s external debt burden. In 2018, private sector nonguaranteed debt was equivalent to about 79.8 per cent of public and publicly guaranteed external debt. By 2025, it had increased to 87.3 per cent. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s total external debt, covering government borrowing, private companies’ foreign loans and short-term obligations, increased from $46.238 billion in 2018 to $145.015 billion in 2025. The report also highlighted the high cost of borrowing from private foreign lenders. According to the World Bank, new loans obtained by Nigeria from private foreign creditors in 2025 attracted an average interest rate of 9.6 per cent, compared with 1.9 per cent for loans from official creditors such as governments and multilateral institutions. Private lenders also offered an average repayment period of 12 years, compared with 25 years for official creditors. The post Nigeria’s private sector foreign debt rise 179.6% to $54.5bn — World Bank appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Watch- Jaylen Brown snubs Jayson Tatum before Celtics crush 76ers 123-101
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Jaylen Brown appeared to brush off Jayson Tatum’s attempt to embrace him before the Boston Celtics faced the Philadelphia 76ers, adding another awkward moment to the attention surrounding the pair’s relationship. Footage from before tip-off showed Tatum approaching Brown for a handshake or embrace. However, Brown remained focused on the basketball in his hands, prompting Tatum to tap him on the chest before giving him a brief side hug. The moment came ahead of another meeting between two Eastern Conference rivals. Boston eventually cruised to a 123-101 victory in Philadelphia, improving its record to 9-2 while the 76ers fell to 9-3. Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum share awkward pre-game moment before Boston Celtics beat Philadelphia 76ers Tatum appeared keen to acknowledge his teammate before the game, but Brown did not immediately reciprocate the gesture. After tapping Brown on the chest and giving him a light hug from the side, Tatum moved on and embraced LeBron James. The interaction quickly attracted attention, particularly given the reported tension surrounding the relationship between the two Celtics stars. However, the footage alone does not establish the reason for Brown’s reaction. Once the game got underway, Tatum finished with 21 points, six rebounds and four assists in 32 minutes. Brown recorded 13 points, five rebounds and two assists across 26 minutes. Boston also received an impressive contribution from Paul George, who led all scorers with 36 points for Philadelphia’s opponents. Payton Pritchard added 18 points while Anfernee Simons contributed 17 for the 76ers. Tyrese Maxey finished with 24 points for Philadelphia, while Joel Embiid managed 16. The Celtics dominated the fourth quarter, outscoring the 76ers 32-19 to turn a competitive contest into a convincing 22-point victory. The two teams are scheduled to meet again later in the regular season, with Brown set for another opportunity to face Philadelphia in what remains an important Eastern Conference rivalry. item.title: 2027: Security tops as APC-PCC unveils 4-point manifesto
item.description: By Soni Daniel, Emma Ujah & Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—The Presidency yesterday asked Nigerians to study the past and current manifestoes of the All Progressives Congress, APC, and judge the party by the promises it has kept since 2023 when it assumed power. Read Also: Security of lives and property to top Tinubu’s agenda in 2nd term – APC The Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, also said President Bola Tinubu will pay priority attention to protection of lives and property if he wins the presidential election on January 16, 2027. Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, who made the declaration at the unveiling of the APC manifesto, titled ‘’From Reforms to Prosperity,’’ described the manifesto as a binding pact with the electorate. “A manifesto, in its strictest sense, is simply a contract between the people and their leaders. It is an inviolable contract, and we take the strict interpretation of what a manifesto represents as gospel under this administration,” he said. He admitted that the reforms had put real pressure on households, adding that the people living through it deserve to be heard. “Nobody should have to pretend that life is easy at the moment,” he said. The former House of Representatives’ Speaker, nonetheless, defended President Tinubu’s decision to act, saying the President confronted the subsidy burden and a distorted foreign exchange system when he took responsibility for the country in 2023. He said: “Leaving those problems untouched would have continued to weaken our ability to invest in the future. The difference between a politician and a leader is that while a politician thinks about the next election, a leader thinks about the next generation. And that is exactly what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated. Four pillars The manifesto rests on four pillars, including a secure and resilient nation; a better quality and more affordable life for every Nigerian; energy, infrastructure and economic growth; and effective and accountable governance. They are tied to the eight priority areas of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which the document said would be carried out on four foundations – macroeconomic stability; the rule of law; institutional capability; and national cohesion. By 2031, the document commits to power generation scaled towards 10,000 megawatts, annual economic growth of six per cent, and youth unemployment and out-of-school children, both halved. It also promises 20,000 additional teachers and health insurance expanded from more than 23 million enrollees to 40 per cent of Nigerians. Primary health centres will function in at least 90 per cent of facilities, up from the current 53 per cent. It further promises to work towards 200,000 homes under the Tinubu Mass Social Housing Scheme, Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria, FMBN, mortgages and licensed private developers, tracked on a public dashboard. item.title: How 76ers star Jaylen Brown performed in marquee showdown vs. Celtics
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images How 76ers star Jaylen Brown performed in marquee showdown vs. Celtics appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jaylen Brown ’s first game against his former team did not go the way the Philadelphia 76ers had hoped. In a matchup circled on calendars since his offseason trade , Brown and the Sixers were blown out 123-101 by the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night. Brown finished with 13 points on 4-of-9 shooting from the field in 25 minutes and 49 seconds of action. He also picked up four personal fouls, while former teammate Jayson Tatum outscored him with 21 points on 8-of-17 shooting. The night started with plenty of intrigue, as Brown appeared to brush off a pregame greeting from Tatum before the two shared a brief side hug. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Once the game began, Brown came out aggressive. He had eight points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals in the first half, going 2-of-4 from the field and 4-of-6 from the free-throw line. Tatum had an answer for him early, though. In the first quarter, the Celtics star stayed in front of his longtime teammate and poked the ball loose to force a turnover and give Boston the ball back . Boston took a 62-51 lead into halftime and never looked back. The Celtics outscored Philadelphia 32-19 in the fourth quarter and led by as many as 29 points. Brown added just five points after the break. Instead, it was Paul George who stole the show. George, who was sent to Boston in the deal that landed Brown in Philadelphia, poured in 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting against his former team . Brown had made it clear before the game that he was not interested in mending fences with Tatum . “There’s nothing to talk about. He’s on his side, I’m on my side,” he said. The loss dropped the Sixers to 9-3 on the season, while the Celtics improved to 9-2. Brown will get another crack at his old team soon enough. The 76ers and Celtics meet again on Jan. 21 in Boston, which will mark Brown’s return to TD Garden. item.title: Pochettino’s $10 Million Price Tag For Manchester United Would Be A Steal
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - United States Press Conference - Seattle Stadium, Seattle, Washington, U.S. - July 5, 2026 U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino during the press conference IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Steven Bisig Manchester United faces a simple choice: stay stuck in the relegation zone or pay the price to fix it. The 54-year-old Mauricio Pochettino has a release clause in his USMNT contract that sits at just $10 million. This figure comes from The Athletic and looks like a bargain for a club valued at $7.2 billion according to reports. Manchester United executives are reviewing Michael Carrick’s future, with a meeting involving minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe scheduled for Wednesday. No final decision has been made, but Carrick is increasingly under pressure. If they pull the trigger, they have the cash to bring Pochettino home to Old Trafford immediately. The Math Makes Sense The cost of buying out Pochettino is low relative to the value of the job. The Athletic reports the $10 million fee covers his release, though assistant coaches cost several million more. The team’s total bill would remain low despite the additional costs, and the club is the third-most valuable soccer team in the world. Real Madrid leads the pack at $9.5 billion, followed by Barcelona at $7.5 billion. United can stomach this bill without breaking their bank or needing a bailout. The financial gap between the USMNT deal and a Premier League return is massive. Pochettino made about $7 million annually with the USMNT. United could provide him with a boatload of money on top of that via a move. One Fox Sports analyst noted the irony of the situation. “Why would he leave the U.S. for something like this? He’s made a lot of money!” they said. But money changes minds. If you throw enough cash at any situation, everybody can be available. United has the funds to make this happen. Players Want Him To Stay The USMNT squad is still focused on their upcoming games against Haiti. Many top players arrived in metro Atlanta on Tuesday, unaware of the rumors until they hit the news. Despite the noise, the team says they will keep working hard. “We’re all very good at just focusing on the next task at hand,” Robinson added. Young stars like Cavan Sullivan are grateful for Pochettino’s guidance. “Mauricio has taken me under his wing in the most tremendous way possible,” Sullivan told a reporter when asked about the manager. The players love him and do not want the drama to distract them. “Everybody loves him,” Sullivan said. They plan to play for him until told otherwise. This loyalty shows why a sudden exit hurts the program, even if the money is right. The Clock Is Ticking United cannot wait forever to make a move. The club is staring at an unfathomable drop to the second division if they get relegated. This has not happened at Old Trafford since 1974. item.title: Cy Ranch returns to Class 6A Division I state volleyball semifinals with win over Clear Springs
item.description: The Cypress Ranch volleyball team poses for a group photo after defeating Clear Springs in the Class 6A Division I Region III final at Delmar Field House in Houston on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026. (Raquel Natalicchio/Houston Chronicle) As Saniyah Reynolds rose above the net and hammered the final kill into the hardwood court at Delmar Fieldhouse, the celebration commenced for the Cypress Ranch volleyball team. It had been 364 days since the Mustangs clinched their first appearance in the UIL state semifinals. Now they're starting to make it an annual tradition. Cy Ranch is headed back to the Class 6A Division I semifinals following a 25-21, 29-27, 25-17 victory against Clear Springs in the Region III final on Tuesday night. "It's a special group," Cy Ranch coach Collea McKinney said. "I said that about last year, too, but these girls … I love our program from our girls all the way to our parents. It's definitely a community effort, and everybody coming together is what made this happen. I know we started building last year, but the girls this year got the see that, and they're like ‘OK, that goal is attainable.' Now we're trying to go all the way, so I'm really excited." HIGHLIGHT A GREAT ATHLETE : Nominate a Houston high school performer for Athlete of The Week Cy Ranch (39-7) has won 28 consecutive matches since dropping four straight in tournament play at the end of August against some elite competition. The Mustangs suffered all seven of their losses within the first 18 matches of the season and have been lights-out since working through those growing pains. Entering Tuesday night, the six teams that had beaten the Mustangs boasted a combined .804 winning percentage. Cy Ranch has dropped just one set through the first four rounds of the playoffs, that coming during a win over Dawson in the regional semifinals. "After last year, we were doubted a lot because we lost a lot of people," said junior outside hitter Sade Bello, a University of Kansas commit who entered the night with more than 600 kills after previously playing alongside her sister, Zora, a senior leader for last year's team. "But just knowing who we are and knowing who we have on this team, we know we can go as far as we did last year or even better if we can just stay disciplined and play our game." Cy Ranch will play the Region IV champion, either Round Rock (35-11) or Lake Travis (41-6), at 4 p.m. Saturday back at Delmar Fieldhouse. Those teams were set to play each other later Tuesday. The Mustangs lost 2-0 against both earlier this season, but McKinney said her players are better now for some of the struggles they faced early on. "I think a lot of growth happened during that time," McKinney said. "It was hard. The girls had to learn each other. During that time, it's pretty much a brand-new team if you look at our roster from last year to this year. They were learning how each other work, how to talk to each other and all the little things. item.title: Celtics’ Paul George hilariously gives 76ers fans the finger after dominant win
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Celtics’ Paul George hilariously gives 76ers fans the finger after dominant win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . For all the talk about the simmering beef between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown, it was Paul George , the player the Boston Celtics acquired from the Philadelphia 76ers in the Brown trade, who proved to be the biggest star of the show. George finished with 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting from the field, and he hit some daggers in the fourth quarter to blow the game wide open en route to a 123-101 win over the 76ers. In the fourth, it looks as though George was drawing inspiration from the animosity he was receiving from a few 76ers fans. In fact, during one pause in the action, the Celtics star subtly and hilariously gave a fan the middle finger just to rub it into their faces. Paul George flips off the Philly crowd 😂 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) (via @NoaDalzell ) pic.twitter.com/YQ11X9HPRR — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 11, 2026 76ers fans are some of the most passionate in the world, and with the game getting out of hand in the fourth, getting George riled up did not help matters whatsoever. After Payton Pritchard drained two straight threes to start the quarter to push the Celtics’ lead to 15, George saw the opportunity to deliver the killing blows to the 76ers. He pulled up for a triple to extend their lead to 18, and then he was clearly feeling himself as he drained a difficult turnaround and-one jumper and made the free throw to push their lead to 21. He would then score five more points to extend his personal run to eight, and by then, the 76ers were out of the game completely. George is experiencing a career revival in Beantown; after his 36-point outing against his former team, he is now averaging 22.0 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 3.8 assists per contest on the year. He’s also playing elite defense, and he looks like he’s at least back to the form he showed during the latter part of his tenure with the Los Angeles Clippers. Keeping him healthy is going to be key for the Celtics, as they are unstoppable when the 36-year-old forward is playing like this and even flipping opposing fans off in the process. Related: Nick Nurse gives Celtics’ Paul George props for 36-point performance against the 76ers Related: Paul George gets 100% real on why things didn’t work with 76ers

item.title: Breaking Down the Kings’ Decision to Move on from Nique Clifford
item.description: Sacramento Kings guard Nique Clifford (10) warms up before the game against the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Sacramento Kings ’ decision to part ways with Nique Clifford could confuse fans, especially given what they sacrificed to land him. Clifford came into the fold with high hopes as a young building block for the franchise, but it didn’t work out as planned. Even though last season was his rookie campaign, Clifford failed to capitalize on the chances he was given and became an afterthought in the rotation. The Kings parted ways with Clifford for two second-round picks, and he is now on the way to OKC. Clifford Didn’t Make the Most of Opportunities One of the major factors pushing Sacramento to cut ties with Clifford was his failure to establish himself in Doug Christie’s rotation this season, despite the Kings’ struggles . Although Clifford is only at the beginning of his professional basketball career, the team wanted to see improvement from a prospect who had shown promise in the past. Whether it was production, contribution, consistency, or being a solid asset when he had minutes on the court, he failed to show he would consistently bring anything useful to the squad. One key factor indicating how much the team lost trust in Clifford is that other players were able to pass him in the rotation. To be more exact, both Daeqwon Plowden and Emmanuel Sharp became those players who got chances to play over Clifford. In addition, the emergence of Leaky Black became yet another player who moved ahead of Clifford in the Sacramento hierarchy. For a prospect expected to be among the team’s younger core players, the news was hardly good. Sacramento Kings guard Nique Clifford (10) shoots the ball against Los Angeles Clippers center Brook Lopez (11) during the third quarter at Intuit Dome. Photo Credit: Kiyoshi Mio, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Heading Back to OKC Perhaps the hardest aspect of the entire scenario for Kings fans to deal with is Clifford’s move to the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Thunder have proven themselves to be one of the best NBA franchises at nurturing young talent and finding players who fit its system. Clifford’s ability to find his place on another team is therefore especially difficult for the people of Sacramento to digest. Nobody wants to see their former Kings prospect blossom into an NBA player after being traded by them. Another reason Clifford’s departure is hard to cope with is that Sacramento had to give up something substantial to draft him with the No. 24 pick in 2025. The Kings sent a 2027 first-round pick (top-16 pick via San Antonio) to Oklahoma City to land him. Future first-round picks are considered highly valuable assets, especially for an NBA team looking to build for the coming years. item.title: Paul George Outplays Jaylen Brown in First Battle of Celtics-76ers Trade Centerpieces
item.description: Paul George Outplays Jaylen Brown in First Battle of Celtics-76ers Trade Centerpieces originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Plenty of basketball fans were excited to watch the individual battle between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown on Tuesday, but another star forward stole the show. Paul George scored a game-high 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting from the field in the Celtics ' 123-101 win over the 76ers, helping his team jump to the top of the Eastern Conference standings. George, who landed in Boston as part of the offseason trade that sent Brown to Philadelphia, had 14 of his 36 points in the fourth quarter, and the Celtics outscored the Sixers 32-19 in the final frame. "What I've learned is, I'm a little bit better with more usage," George said during an appearance on NBC's postgame show. "That's not a knock to my opportunities here in Philly. Quite frankly, I wasn't healthy [enough] to take on the workload. "Here in Boston, they gave me an opportunity to come out and play and be myself. Joe [Mazzulla] has integrated me right into the offense and allowed me to just be myself." Paul George put on a SHOW in his return to Philly! ☘️ 36 PTS 14-22 FG 6-11 3-PT FG 1 WIN https://t.co/H8dKUiECIn — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) November 11, 2026 That performance continued an impressive start for George, who noted that his body is "holding up wonderfully" after dealing with multiple injuries in his two seasons with the 76ers. Heading into the rivalry matchup, he was averaging 20.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.3 steals per game while shooting 42.5 percent from 3-point range. "The beauty of this offense is the game is just gonna find me," George said. "That's one thing Joe preaches within our offense, just let it find you. I'm not pressing. I'm not rushing. I'm not forcing. I've always played that game, and my best nights have come from me just letting the game happen. That's when I'm at my best." Brown, on the other hand, had a night to forget. He wasn't able to get revenge against his former squad, scoring just 13 points in 26 minutes. Foul trouble limited his impact, as he picked up two fouls in the first quarter. "Just got those two early fouls that kind of distorted my rhythm throughout the whole game and kind of struggled to get it back," Brown said ( via The Philadelphia Inquirer's Chris Hine ). "We had opportunities to get back into the game. It was a tie game at one point. They shot the hell out of the ball, executed well. We gotta get better." The 2024 Finals MVP finished with a plus-minus of minus-27, the worst mark of any player on either team. George had a plus-minus of plus-17. Of course, it's a little early to declare that Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens has already been vindicated for his bold move. For one night, though, George showed exactly why Boston was willing to pull the trigger on such a controversial deal. More Celtics news People Close to Jayson Tatu

item.title: Former Ohio State star has one word to describe the Buckeyes loss
item.description: Credit: Vincent Carchietta-USA TODAY Sports Ohio State’s blowout loss to Oregon has drawn plenty of criticism from Buckeyes fans and former players alike. And two of the program’s former stars are among the most frustrated. Former Ohio State running back Beanie Wells called the loss “embarrassing,” taking particular aim at the Buckeyes’ defense, as national champion quarterback Cardale Jones agreed with that assessment. Ohio State’s Collapse Ohio State jumped out to a 14-0 lead against Oregon on Saturday, but the Ducks scored 38 straight points on their way to a 41-28 win. It was the Buckeyes’ second straight loss after falling 30-18 at USC, and it was their first time losing back-to-back games to unranked opponents since 1992. Former Buckeyes blasted the team after the game, and Barstool’s Brandon Walker said that Ryan Day is “doing the worst job of his entire career.” Ohio State then fired Discher just nine games into his first season, and Day said this week that Luke Fahey will remain the starter against Northwestern. ‘There’s no bullets flying’ When host Dave Holmes of The Script podcast asked the pair of former Buckeyes for their reactions to Ohio State’s loss this week, Wells didn’t hold back. “Oh, it’s wild. And, you know, I use the word a little bit loosely at times, but this is, you know, very much indeed what it is: embarrassing,” Wells said on The Script . “When you look at the performances that we’ve had in these big matchups, when you look at the inability to be able to get to the passer, be able to stop plays on third down, and more importantly, just be able to stop explosive gains. I mean, that’s not Ohio State football.” “When we talk about Ohio State defenses, we typically talk about the Silver Bullets. Well, there’s no bullets flying. I think we all are out of bullets at this point in time,” Wells continued. Jones argued that Ohio State’s defensive numbers were inflated by weak competition, and that the Buckeyes keep coming up short against good teams. “We were stacking up against those top defenses because we was going against really bad offenses,” Jones said. “We continue to fall short in these big matchups of recently. So that is an issue of concern.” Needless to say, some of the program’s former players are just as frustrated as the fans. The post Former Ohio State star has one word to describe the Buckeyes loss appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: “Lack Of Connectivity”: Jon Scheyer Offers No Filter After Duke Makes Headlines For All The Wrong Reasons vs Michigan State
item.description: November 4, 2025: Duke Blue Devils head coach Jon Scheyer check the clock during the first half against the Texas Longhorns in the Dick Vitale Invitational matchup at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, NC. /CSM Charlotte United States – ZUMAc04_ 20251104_zma_c04_107 Copyright: xScottxKinserx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Duke walked into Chicago ranked No. 2, with one of the deepest rosters in college basketball and a coach who said he wanted his team tested. Hours later, the Blue Devils had been tested, and they did not pass. For the first time this season, Duke lost, and Jon Scheyer did not try to dress it up. After Duke fell to Michigan State 79-73, Scheyer admitted his team had been outplayed. “They outplayed us in every facet of the game, I thought. Our lack of connectivity on offense was not good enough. We’re going to fix it. We have things to address and we’ll fix it. It’s a long season ahead,” he said. The final score told only part of the story. Michigan State never allowed Duke to take the lead at any point in the 40 minutes, keeping the Blue Devils chasing from the opening tip. When a coach goes unfiltered, the real problems surface. Subscribe to stay on top of Duke's struggles and what Scheyer's candid assessment reveals about the team's future. And the Spartans made sure that chase started early. They made their first four shots and ripped off an 11-2 run, forcing Scheyer to call a timeout just 2:33 into the game. Duke turned the ball over four times in the first three minutes, and nothing seemed to fall. The Blue Devils missed 11 of their first 13 shots and went 0-of-8 from three-point range to start. By halftime, Duke had made just 7-of-27 shots, while Michigan State carried a 34-25 lead into the break. That early struggle eventually became the bigger problem Scheyer pointed to: Duke’s lack of connectivity on offense. The Blue Devils had looked smooth in their first two games, averaging 98.5 points while shooting a combined 55%. Against Michigan State, however, the ball stopped moving with the same rhythm. Duke finished with 13 turnovers and shot 33.3% overall (20 of 60) and about 24% from three. John Blackwell led Duke with 17 points, but it took him 16 shots to get there. Deron Rippey Jr., meanwhile, went 1 of 5. Michigan State deserves plenty of credit for that offensive breakdown. The Spartans played the kind of defense that makes even a talented team look lost. Jordan Scott, a 6-foot-8 sophomore, recorded six of Michigan State’s eight blocks, doing so after never having more than two in a game. Five of those came in the first half alone. While Scott protected the paint, Jeremy Fears Jr. took charge on the other end. He finished with 18 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds. He already had eight assists by halftime and scored or assisted on 22 of Michigan State’s 34 first-half points. The Spartans’ bench also outscored Duke’s 35-28. item.title: 10 Takeaways: Avalanche’s Veterans Made Their Presence Felt in Toronto
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What a night for some of the Avalanche’s most experienced players. Gabe Landeskog , Devon Toews , Brock Nelson, and Nazem Kadri were all instrumental in helping Colorado open its road trip with a 6-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs. Read Next Postgame Reaction: Devon Toews Is Giving the Avalanche Another Offensive Weapon 10 Takeaways 1. Landeskog has had an interesting start to the season. He looked slow during the early portions of the schedule but started to pick things up offensively from time to time. In recent games, it feels like the captain has found all sorts of ways to be effective. His fight against Moritz Seider on Saturday at Ball Arena was one of the highlights of the night. Three days later, he scored twice, including the game-winner, to lead Colorado past Toronto. Landeskog now has seven goals and 12 points in 19 games. He’s on pace for more than 50 points over a full season, which would be massive for him at this stage of his career. 2. How about that pass from Kadri on Landeskog’s game-winning goal? It helped that none of Toronto’s defenders challenged him behind the net, but Kadri still had to thread the needle. He sent a pass through the blue paint to find Landeskog in front, with the puck slipping between goalie Sergei Bobrovsky and defenseman Darren Raddysh. It came just 51 seconds after Jack Roslovic tied the game at 3-3. That’s an impressive response, and Kadri deserves credit for the helper. 3. I highlighted this in my postgame reaction, but Toews’ offensive production has been a major factor in Colorado getting more out of its defensemen. Head coach Jared Bednar separated Toews and Cale Makar shortly after Josh Manson’s injury , putting Toews with Sam Malinski and Makar with Brett Kulak. The results have been encouraging. Toews has continued producing, Makar has picked up his offensive game, and Malinski has started contributing more consistently. It’s given Colorado a different look on the back end without sacrificing the offense it expects from its top blueliners. 4. Oh yeah, the Avs won 6-3 in Toronto, and Toews finished the night with a +5 rating. 5. Malinski didn’t do much offensively when the season began. He was held without a point through his first five games, which included a healthy scratch in Calgary. Since then, he’s slowly worked his way back into a rhythm. In his last eight games, Malinski has six assists. He still hasn’t found the back of the net, but he’s getting more comfortable and showing more of the offensive instincts from a season ago. He finished with an assist and was +3 against the Maple Leafs on Tuesday night. 6. Continuing with the veteran contributions, Nelson scored Colorado’s first goal on a play that started on Jaden Schwartz ‘ stick. Nelson buried his fifth of the season to tie things at 1-1 after the Avalanche fell behind early. It was an important response from a team that hasn’t always done a great job of recovering after surrendering the first goal

item.title: Jaylen Brown takes the high road after struggling vs. Celtics: 'Credit to Jayson'
item.description: Jaylen Brown takes the high road after struggling vs. Celtics: 'Credit to Jayson' originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jaylen Brown insisted he had no beef — but maybe some "lamb chops" — with former teammate Jayson Tatum. An icy interaction between the two before tip-off on Tuesday might have said otherwise, but once basketball became the focus, the two kept it professional. Tatum and Brown played the game without incident, but one of them decisively had the better night. Tatum and the Celtics rolled to a 123-101 win, with Brown struggling as the 76ers fell behind. After the game, Brown took the high road and explained the awkward pre-game interaction with his former Celtics co-star. Here's a look at what Brown had to say. NOH: Jaylen Brown's revenge game showed worrying cracks in 76ers Jaylen Brown discusses Jayson Tatum face-off Brown told reporters after the loss that he "wasn't paying attention" when Tatum approached him and put his arms around him moments before tip-off. "I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else is just ... to be honest, I wasn't paying attention." On a night in which he struggled mightily, Brown gave credit to his former teammate by name. "Credit to Jayson. He played well tonight," Brown said. "Credit to the Celtics." Jaylen Brown postgame on the foul trouble that affected his night, what he was feeling coming into the night, and his response when asked about the pre-tip moment with Jayson Tatum. https://t.co/XNSRuWmRSv — Chris Hine (@ChristopherHine) November 11, 2026 Tatum wasn't the focal point for the Celtics, as his 21 points on 8-of-17 from the field paled in comparison to Paul George's 36-point outburst, but he did play better than Brown. The 76ers star didn't reach double-digit points until late in the fourth quarter, scoring 13 points on 4-of-9 from the field and finishing a team-worst -27. After the loss, Brown admitted he was "frustrated" with his performance. "I wanted to perform better for my team," Brown said. "Foul trouble kind of derailed me a little bit, but you know, it happens." Joel Embiid, LeBron James and VJ Edgecombe all struggled offensively as well, so the loss certainly wasn't all on Brown, but the contrast between Brown's tough night and George's outstanding performance was stark after the two were traded for each other in the summer. MORE: Inside beef between Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown

item.title: Thunder’s Chet Holmgren is already taking shots before games amid knee injury
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Thunder’s Chet Holmgren is already taking shots before games amid knee injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Oklahoma City Thunder are going through a challenging stretch, as they are playing sans three starters, Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren , and Cason Wallace, for an extended period due to major injuries, threatening to disrupt their momentum and test the roster’s depth. But while Williams and Wallace have yet to resume basketball activities, Holmgren was seen participating in the Thunder’s shootaround before facing the Portland Trail Blazers at Moda Center on Tuesday. Holmgren is out due to a knee injury. The Oklahoman’s Justin Hernandez shared a video of Holmgren, in workout gear, getting up shots , although he was moving economically. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Chet Holmgren made the trip and is getting some shots up before tonight’s game,” wrote Hernandez on X. “He was given a timeline of eight to 10 weeks on October 30 to recover from a small patellar tendon tear.” Chet Holmgren made the trip and is getting some shots up before tonight’s game. He was given a timeline of 8-to-10 weeks on Oct. 30 to recover from a small patellar tendon tear. pic.twitter.com/3cJUfxwiFA — Justin Martinez (@Justintohoops) November 11, 2026 It is definitely a sign that the 24-year-old center is on the right track, although his return remains unclear. The Thunder have played well without Holmgren, Williams, and Wallace. They are gunning for their fifth straight victory against the Trail Blazers. Still, obviously, the team would rather have its key players back on the floor as soon as possible. Williams has an ankle injury, while Wallace has a shoulder injury. After Holmgren went down, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was at a loss for words , underscoring the Thunder’s worries. But unheralded players have stepped up, including Kenrich Williams, Aday Mara, and Bennett Stirtz, providing support to the remaining core of Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Isaiah Hartenstein, Jared McCain, and Alex Caruso. Entering the game against Portland, Oklahoma City is third in the Western Conference with an 8-2 record. Related: Thunder waive recently signed player to complete Nique Clifford trade

item.title: 2027 South Side Sox Top Prospect No. 90: Carson Jacobs
item.description: Somewhat sparse summer work for Carson Jacobs keeps him near the bottom of our Top 100. | ﻿(Photo by Hannah Bachman/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) Carson Jacobs Right-Handed Relief Pitcher 6´9´´ 215 pounds Age: 26 2025 South Side Sox Top 100 Prospect Ranking 71 2026 South Side Sox Top Prospect Ranking 86 2026 High Level Birmingham (AA) Age relative to high level -0.6 years SSS rank among all right-handed relievers in the system 15 Overall 2026 season stats 2-2 ⚾️ 32 games (7 finishes) ⚾️ 43 2/3 IP ⚾️ 3.71.ERA ⚾️ 62 K ⚾️ 43 BB ⚾️ 1.695 WHIP ⚾️ 0.7 WAR If you’re jumping center against 6´9´´behemoth Carson Jacobs, you know what you’re in for. Facing him in the batter’s box, against a reach that releases the ball close enough to tickle your chin, is another matter entirely. Jacobs has used his height to great advantage in his year-and-change in the White Sox system. The White Sox ignored his stats at the baseball hotbed of North Dakota State University in 2023 (2-5, 34 innings, 6.62 ERA) and snapped him up immediately after the draft as a UDFA. With no inhibitions, the club put the tall righty right to work, and its confidence paid off handsomely, as Jacobs busted out 6 1⁄3 innings while allowing just one earned run. Despite that small sample size greatness, it’s only fair the White Sox packed Jacobs back up for a repeat ACL tour to start 2024 — and it was only fair Jacobs murdered ACL batters once more (3.22 ERA in 22 1⁄3 innings, plus his first pro save). From there, Jacobs did time in both Kannapolis and Winston-Salem, ending the year with a sparkling 2.37 ERA over 31 games. With 19 of those games being finishes, it’s clear the White Sox want to slot Jacobs in as a setup/closer short man. While Jacobs had been killing it through his first two summers with the Sox, 2025 turned out to be another matter entirely. The righty’s peripherals held steady, except for one key spot: Hitters caught up to him, with a dramatic increase in hits per nine (5.7 H/9 in 2024, up to 8.4). That’s a worrying sign, as Jacobs was age-appropriate for High-A, where he pitched all but two of his games. One bright spot for the reliever is that the White Sox thought highly enough of him in spite of a rough 2025 to send him on an audition to the Arizona Fall League. There, Jacobs saw action in eight games to a 4.50 ERA — and he was lucky to get away with just that, having walked 11 batters for a 16.5 BB/9. Jacobs tasted Double-A for two games in 2025, and jumped right back to Double-A for 2026. And, back with the Barons, he was used somewhat sparingly. He never spent time on the IL, at least officially, but didn’t even make his season debut until the end of April. And in spite of relieving all year, his rest between appearances often more closely resembled a rotation arm, sitting for upwards of a week between games. When he was on the mound, Jacobs was stingier with contact, but offset that with a wild streak that raised his overall WHIP. Bottom line, though, Jacobs im

item.title: Where the Pirates Stand With Brandon Lowe’s Free Agency
item.description: The key narrative surrounding the Pittsburgh Pirates since the offseason began has been Brandon Lowe’s free agency. Re-signing the 32-year-old is unequivocally the team's biggest priority this offseason. The All-Star second baseman was arguably the team’s best all-around player in 2026 and one of the key reasons for their 11-win improvement from the year before. However, after just one year in Pittsburgh, there’s a chance Lowe could move on to a new city. That said, Pirates general manager Ben Cherington said on Tuesday at the GM Meeting in Las Vegas that the team has had conversations with Lowe and his agent, and they’ve been “good." Cherington also reiterated that he hopes Lowe ends up back with the Pirates next year, but the sides are taking it one step at a time. As far as any other details are concerned, that’s where Lowe’s free agency with the Pirates stands right now. It may not be the news many were hoping for, but it was available just a few days ago: Lowe and the Pirates are talking, but no new deal appears imminent based on the executives' comments. Whether a deal actually gets done remains to be seen. May 9, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Pittsburgh Pirates infielder Brandon Lowe (5) hits a two RBI double against the San Francisco Giants during the ninth inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Robert Edwards-Imagn Images Another important piece to Lowe’s free agency is that the Pirates did extend the qualifying offer to him about a week ago. That represents a one-year deal worth $23.15 million. If anything, Pittsburgh offering that contract to the free agent at least signals that the front office is serious about bringing him back. (The extra draft pick if Lowe signs elsewhere doesn’t hurt, either.) Lowe has until November 17 to either accept or decline the qualifying offer from the Pirates. Even if it is declined, that wouldn’t rule out a return to Pittsburgh. Just as the Pirates are actively trying to re-sign Lowe, other teams across baseball are getting into the mix, too, and the competition for the prized free agent appears to be heating up. Earlier in the week, it was reported that several American League East teams , namely the Boston Red Sox, New York Yankees, and Toronto Blue Jays, had some level of interest in Lowe. All three teams need a second baseman, and Lowe is the best on the market. Where Lowe ends up signing this offseason is still anyone’s guess. Cherington confirmed he’s had talks with Lowe’s agent about staying in Pittsburgh, but that doesn’t guarantee he’s still a Pirate on Opening Day.

item.title: Paul George celebrates being more impactful in Boston compared to his time in Philadelphia
item.description: Paul George celebrates being more impactful in Boston compared to his time in Philadelphia originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It was a big game for the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night because it was the long-awaited blockbuster game against the Philadelphia 76ers . Of course, the primary story was the Jayson Tatum vs Jaylen Brown matchup, but Paul George had something to say about that. George was the primary trade piece that went to Boston after the Brown trade. Considering George never really got it going in Philly, he made sure to let them know that he is in the right place now. Paul George loves his role in Boston compared to his role in Philly George has been good to start the season with the Celtics because he looks completely healthy. However, he had his best game of the year so far with a massive performance against his former team. The 36-year-old forward was the best player on the floor, posting 36 points on 14-of-22 from the field. It was one of the best performances of any player this season because it felt like he could not miss. MORE: The Jaylen Brown-Paul George trade is looking like a win-win decision George attributes this performance to having an optimal role with the Celtics. Before the 2026-27 season even started, George admitted that Jayson Tatum is the best player on the Celtics, but he would do everything he can to help the team win, and that's what he did against the 76ers . "I know what I can bring to the table when I'm healthy; I know what I'm capable of. That was the biggest thing that was frustrating in the past 2 years: people thinking that I lost my game. I just wasn't healthy, and I was trying to play through stuff," George said in his post-game interview with the NBC crew . As long as George is playing like this, the Celtics' potential is quite high. It will be tough to keep doing it, but it seems that he is healthy and locked in to lead the Celtics as one of the best players. item.title: I was soaked for hours before help came — 74-year-old blind man whose home was wrecked by wind storms
item.description: …Good-spirited man begins rebuilding the house By Chinedu Adonu ENUGU – For 74-year-old Mr. Stephen Ogbo, the rainstorm that ripped through his residence at Ugbo Ezeji, D-Line, Abakpa Nike, Enugu metropolis, was a terrifying, unforgettable experience. The ugly incident left him soaked in water for hours, trapped in a shattered building and unable to find his way to safety because of his blindness. As the storm raged, Ogbo could neither see the destruction around him nor find his way out. He remained helpless until an unidentified female tenant eventually came to his rescue. Recounting his ordeal, Ogbo said the woman approached him after he had spent several hours soaked in water, unable to escape from the disaster. “The female tenant came to me after several hours but couldn’t find any way to escape as a blind man. She said: “Daddy, we have been trapped by the windstorm,” he recalled. According to him, the woman held him, led him out of the destroyed building, and searched for shelter where he could find safety. Although he could not identify his rescuer, he remembered that the voice belonged to a woman. “I do not know the name of the woman who came to my rescue, but the voice was a woman’s voice,” he said. A native of Nomeh Unateze in Nkanu East Local Government Area of Enugu State, Ogbo said he had lived in the compound for about eight years before the incident. The rainstorm damaged the residential building housing 23 families, ripping off its roof and destroying property belonging to tenants. The incident left the occupants struggling to find shelter and salvage their belongings. For the affected families, what began as an ordinary evening quickly turned into a nightmare, with the destruction leaving them with the difficult task of restoring their homes and livelihoods. A cry for help However, days after the incident, help has begun to come following an appeal by the victims for help. Chief Kingsley Chizoba Nweke, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Enugu East Senatorial District, where the blind man hails from, has commenced the reconstruction of the damaged home after watching a video in which the victims appealed for assistance. Nweke visited the affected residents at Ugbo Ezeji and said their plight moved him to intervene, and announced that building materials had been purchased and contractors mobilised to commence the reconstruction. “It’s a pity, actually. If you look at the roof, it is damaged, and the place is messed up. I saw them interviewed two days ago and they cried out that they needed help. “That touched me so much, so I said it was important that I come to their rescue. We have bought the materials, mobilized the contractors, and the work has already commenced,” he said. He explained that the exercise would involve reinforcing the affected structures and replacing damaged roofs to enable the residents to return to their homes. “My priority is to make sure they get back to their houses and keep living a

item.title: FG coming with major agric reforms to boost food production, cut inflation — ADENLE
item.description: The Federal Government (FG) has proposed sweeping reforms in the agricultural sector, including digitalisation, mechanisation and improved coordination among government agencies in the sector, to boost food production, reduce food inflation and strengthen food security. Senior Special Adviser on Agricultural Innovation to the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Professor Ademola Adenle, disclosed this in an interview where he outlined plans to resolve long-standing challenges in the sector. Adenle said digitalisation will help government identify genuine farmers, monitor production, ensure transparent distribution of inputs and expand farmers’ access to markets. He said the National Agricultural Growth initiative had introduced a system where agro-dealers distribute inputs to verified farmers while monitoring their output. According to him, the intervention has increased production by 30%, with wheat output rising from 420,000 tonnes to 480,000 tonnes annually. He, however, admitted that higher production alone would not bring down food prices unless institutional weaknesses and structural inefficiencies were addressed. “Previous programmes focused mainly on production and input distribution without addressing institutional capacity, food security and agro-industrialisation,” he said. Adenle called for an overhaul of the ministry’s administrative and legal structures, noting that bureaucratic bottlenecks had limited the impact of interventions. He identified poor coordination among federal, state and local governments as a major challenge, and advocated harmonised agricultural policies across the three tiers. He also proposed performance-based financing, annual key performance indicators, stronger monitoring and evaluation, data-driven decision-making, and legislation to promote accountability and transparency. On rising food prices, Adenle blamed illegal movement of produce across Nigeria’s borders and hoarding of food commodities for creating artificial scarcity. He said the Nigeria Customs Service and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission are working with security agencies to address the problem. The post FG coming with major agric reforms to boost food production, cut inflation — ADENLE appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Climate plans: CAPPA warns against fossil fuel expansion, corporate capture
item.description: … Says Nigeria’s 2060 net-zero ambition contradicts 3m barrels-per-day oil target … Demands phase-down of fossil fuels, grants, protection of community land rights By Chioma Obinna Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) on Tuesday warned that African governments risk turning their climate commitments into instruments for expanding fossil fuel production and advancing corporate interests at the expense of vulnerable communities. The organisation, alongside the Africa Make Big Polluters Pay Coalition (MBPP Africa), said Africa’s climate transition would amount to little more than rhetoric unless governments confronted the contradictions between their renewable energy commitments, continued investments in oil and gas, and growing dependence on foreign climate financing. The warning came as the organisations unveiled two reports examining Nigeria’s Energy Transition Plan and the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) of five African countries at a media presentation in Lagos. The reports, titled Four Years On: Examining Nigeria’s Just Transition Plan and Nationally Determined Contributions in Africa: A Five-Country Policy Analysis, assessed the climate commitments of Nigeria, Cameroon, South Africa, Togo and Uganda. They identified fossil fuel expansion, uncertain climate financing, carbon markets and the growing influence of private corporations in climate policy development as major threats to achieving a genuinely just transition across the continent. Speaking, the Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said the central question was whether African climate policies were genuinely transforming economies and protecting people or creating fresh opportunities for corporate interests to profit while communities bear the consequences. He said: “These reports emerge from a fundamental concern: Are Africa’s climate policies genuinely transforming our economies and protecting our people, or are they creating new opportunities for corporate interests to profit while communities bear the consequences?” Oluwafemi said governments could not claim to be pursuing decarbonisation while simultaneously approving projects and infrastructure that entrenched dependence on fossil fuels. He cited the contradictions in Uganda, where French multinational TotalEnergies promotes investments in renewable energy, including solar, while remaining a leading developer of the East African Crude Oil Pipeline, EACOP, and the Tilenga oil project. He also referenced Cameroon’s award of five of nine oil blocks offered to fossil fuel operators, including Murphy Oil and Octavia Energy, despite its stated decarbonisation commitments. In Nigeria, the report identified a major contradiction between the country’s ambition to achieve net-zero emissions by 2060 and its official target of producing three million barrels of crude oil daily by 2030. It acknowledged progress in renewable energy deployment and policy development but argued that the country’s

item.title: Agbazuere backs Otti’s second-term bid after U-turn
item.description: Dismisses alleged anti-Ngwa remark, cautions critics By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who was a vocal critic of Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has declared support for the governor’s re-election bid, saying he deserves a second term. Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed an allegation attributed to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated. Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere cautioned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, warning that defamatory statements could attract legal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act. He said the allegation would not undermine Otti’s support base, particularly among the Ngwa people. “Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. Anybody who wants to say anything should be careful and say what he knows to be true,” he warned. Explaining his support for the governor, Agbazuere said the Otti administration had demonstrated commitment to infrastructure development, urban renewal, workers’ welfare and good governance. He cited the reconstruction of Port Harcourt Road and Bank Road in Aba, the Omenuko Bridge and Arochukwu Road as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive. He also commended the governor for what he described as regular payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities, as well as improvements in allowances for traditional rulers. On criticisms that increased federal allocations should have translated into more development projects, Agbazuere argued that the rising cost of construction materials must be considered. He cited the increase in the price of cement from about ₦2,000 to ₦12,000 per bag as an example of the inflationary pressures facing construction projects. He challenged critics to visit the state and assess ongoing projects rather than evaluate the administration from a distance. Describing Otti as a banker and trained economist, Agbazuere said the governor understood accountability and prudent management of public resources. item.title: How AI is helping Nigerian farmers tackle crop diseases, improve farm decisions
item.description: By Cynthia Alo With many Nigerian farmers still relying on traditional knowledge to identify crop diseases and determine appropriate treatments, delayed access to agricultural advice often means problems are left unresolved until they affect yields. In some cases, farmers have to wait days for agronomists to visit their farms and recommend solutions. CropCura, a digital agricultural innovation co-founded by Victor Onyekachukwu, is seeking to change this practice by bringing crop diagnosis and farm advisory services directly to farmers through technology. Onyekachukwu said the application allows farmers to take pictures of affected crops and receive an AI-powered analysis and recommendations on possible solutions in less than a minute. Apart from crop diagnosis, the platform provides weather information, an AI advisory service and digital farm mapping which allow farmers to access information needed to make decisions about their farms. He said the innovation also addresses another longstanding challenge in Nigerian agriculture which is farmers’ difficulty accessing formal credit because of inadequate records. Through digital farm profiles containing information about farmers, their locations, crops and farm sizes, Onyekachukwu said the technology will also combine a credit-scoring system that can help financial institutions assess farmers for lending. The platform, he said, currently has more than 2,000 farmers, who have mapped over 10,000 hectares of farmland. However, Onyekachukwu identified language barriers, limited smartphone access, low digital literacy and farmers’ distrust of technology as obstacles to wider adoption. He said the government should introduce policies recognising verified digital farm profiles as acceptable evidence for accessing agricultural loans and grants. The post How AI is helping Nigerian farmers tackle crop diseases, improve farm decisions appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Research-policy disconnect undermines agric interventions — Experts
item.description: By Cynthia Alo Agricultural experts have attributed the disconnect between farmers, researchers and policymakers as a major factor undermining the effectiveness of agricultural policies and interventions. This is even as they called for greater farmer participation in research design and policy formulation. According to them, research priorities were often determined without adequate consideration of farmers’ immediate needs, while policy implementation was constrained by funding limitations, institutional bottlenecks and poor communication of research findings. The experts spoke during the virtual inaugural episode of the Agricultural Policy Circle, organised by Farmosphere, with the theme, “Finding the Gap where Research, Policy, and Practice disconnect.” Agriculture researcher, Ifunanya Orisekeh,said research questions were sometimes determined before researchers reached farming communities, leaving farmers to respond to problems that might not reflect their immediate realities. She said research agendas were often shaped by funding calls, academic requirements and institutional timelines, while the time required to generate findings further widened the gap between research and practice. She said: “Research agendas are shaped before a funding call comes up. For example, if there is a project that needs a student already set, by the time you reach the field, the question is already printed and the farmer is there to answer your question. “So we can become very good in the research perspective. We are very good at answering questions that farmers have never asked.” Orisekeh said research could take three to four years to produce findings, by which time the conditions confronting farmers might have changed. She also questioned the practice of measuring project success by the number of farmers trained without establishing whether they continued using the recommended practices after project support ended. Using conservation agriculture as an example, she said, “It is widely promoted and many farmers have widely dropped it as well once the project and even the report is over.” She identified the mismatch between research schedules and farming seasons, inadequate representation of different categories of farmers and failure to return research findings to communities as other weaknesses. Also speaking, Founder of AgricIncome Hub and Chief Executive Officer of Maxipharo Farms, Olaoluwa Farotimi, identified inadequate access to credit, unstable markets, poor extension services, logistics challenges and climate-related risks as major constraints confronting farmers. He said agricultural financing often failed to reflect production cycles, while farmers had little control over market prices and could suffer losses from sudden policy changes. He said: “There is no access to credit for farmers. For example, you have a production cycle of two months or a month, and you have to pay back in six months while your crop is still in the field’’.
